title: The Season That Moved
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、制度、実証結果ではない。登録台帳は制作来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional botanical garden kept a flowering calendar for visitors who hoped to see particular plants during the spring, and for many years its staff printed the same guide with only minor changes.
sentences.ja: 架空の植物園は春に特定植物の花を見たい来園者向けに開花カレンダーを作り、長年わずかな変更だけで同じ案内を印刷した。

sentences.en: When a retired gardener donated notebooks containing observations from earlier decades, the director noticed that the dates recorded for several species differed from those shown in the current guide.
sentences.ja: 引退した園丁が数十年前の観察ノートを寄贈すると、園長は複数種の記録日が現行案内と異なることに気づいた。

sentences.en: Some staff members immediately suggested that the difference revealed a general shift in the seasons, while others wondered whether changes in the garden itself could account for the apparent pattern.
sentences.ja: 一部職員は季節全般の変化を示すとすぐ提案したが、庭園自体の変化で見かけのパターンを説明できるか疑問を持つ者もいた。

sentences.en: Instead of presenting the notebooks as conclusive evidence, the director asked the staff to examine how the observations had originally been made and what information had survived alongside them.
sentences.ja: ノートを決定的証拠とせず当初どのように観察され何の情報が一緒に残ったか調べるよう指示した。

sentences.en: The records revealed that different observers had sometimes described the beginning of flowering in different ways, although their entries appeared to use identical terminology at first glance.
sentences.ja: 記録から、一見同一用語を使っていても観察者によって開花の始まりを異なる方法で記述した場合があると分かった。

sentences.en: One person had noted the appearance of the first open flower on a plant, whereas another recorded the date when a large proportion of the flowers had opened.
sentences.ja: 一人は最初の花の開花を記し、別の人は花の大部分が開いた日を記した。

sentences.en: The staff also discovered that some plants had been moved to new locations and that trees planted nearby had gradually altered the amount of sunlight reaching them.
sentences.ja: 一部の植物が移植され近くの木が届く日光量を徐々に変えていたことも見つかった。

sentences.en: These circumstances complicated comparisons across time without making the historical observations worthless, since the notebooks still contained descriptions that could help establish what had actually been observed.
sentences.ja: これらの事情は時期を超えた比較を難しくしたが、ノートには実際の観察内容を確定する助けになる記述もあり無価値にはしなかった。

sentences.en: The director proposed a new observation protocol that defined several distinct stages of flowering and required staff to document the conditions surrounding each plant during regular visits.
sentences.ja: 園長は開花の複数段階を定義し定期観察時に植物周囲の条件を記録する新手順を提案した。

sentences.en: The garden would preserve the earlier notebooks in their original form while creating a separate collection of records that could be compared more consistently in future years.
sentences.ja: 以前のノートを原形で保存する一方、将来より一貫して比較できる別の記録集を作ることにした。

sentences.en: Staff members discussed whether historical entries could be classified retrospectively, but they agreed to mark uncertain cases instead of assigning a precise category where the description was insufficient.
sentences.ja: 過去記録を事後分類できるか議論したが記述不足の際は正確な分類を割り当てず不確かな事例として記すと合意した。

sentences.en: The project was not intended to establish the causes of any actual environmental change, since the garden and its entire collection of observations were invented for this educational example.
sentences.ja: 庭園と観察記録全てが教材例用の架空設定なので、実際の環境変化の原因を確定する目的ではなかった。

sentences.en: The revised visitor guide no longer promised that a particular species would be flowering on a specific date, but described the period during which visitors might reasonably expect to encounter it.
sentences.ja: 修正版案内は特定日に必ず開花すると約束せず合理的に出会えると期待できる期間を記した。

sentences.en: It also included an explanation of why the appearance of the garden could differ from one year to another without any single observation necessarily representing a permanent change.
sentences.ja: 単一観察が必ずしも恒久変化を表さずとも年によって外観が違い得る理由も説明した。

sentences.en: A small exhibition displayed the old notebooks beside the new observation forms, inviting visitors to compare the kinds of questions that each collection of records could help answer.
sentences.ja: 小展示は旧ノートと新観察用紙を並べ各記録が答える助けとなる問いの種類を比較するよう来園者を招いた。

sentences.en: Rather than concealing the limitations of their historical material, the staff treated those limitations as part of the story of how environmental knowledge is gradually developed.
sentences.ja: 歴史資料の限界を隠さず環境知識が徐々に形成される物語の一部として扱った。

sentences.en: Long-term observations can be particularly valuable precisely because environmental processes may unfold over periods that exceed the duration of an individual research project or a person's working life.
sentences.ja: 長期観察は環境過程が個別研究期間や職業人生を超えて展開し得るからこそ特に有用だ。

sentences.en: Their usefulness, however, depends partly on the ability of later researchers to understand how an observation was defined, under what circumstances it was recorded, and whether its meaning remained consistent.
sentences.ja: しかし有用性は後の研究者が観察の定義、記録時の事情、意味の一貫性を理解できるかにも依存する。

sentences.en: Preserving data therefore involves more than protecting a collection of numbers or dates from physical damage, because information about the production of those records may be equally important.
sentences.ja: 記録生成についての情報も同等に重要になり得るためデータ保存は数や日付の物理損傷を防ぐ以上のことを伴う。

sentences.en: The fictional garden illustrates how an inherited record can become the foundation of a more informative investigation without being treated as an automatically reliable answer to a question it was never designed to address.
sentences.ja: 架空庭園は受け継いだ記録が本来答える意図のなかった問いの自動的に信頼できる答えでなくより有益な調査の基礎となる様子を示す。

vocabulary.definition: in a way that must occur

questions.prompt: What prompted the staff to reconsider the calendar?
options: A request to replace all plants.
questions.explanation_ja: 過去の観察ノートがきっかけ。

questions.prompt: Why did the director avoid an immediate environmental conclusion?
options: Other changes might explain the apparent pattern.
The staff had already established a cause.
questions.explanation_ja: 別の要因を検討する必要。

questions.prompt: How did observers define flowering differently?
options: First open flower versus a large proportion of open flowers.

questions.prompt: Why were the notebooks still useful?
options: Every entry used a uniform method.
They proved a single cause of change.
Descriptions could clarify what had been observed.
questions.explanation_ja: 観察内容の説明が残る。

questions.prompt: What does the new protocol require?
options: Recording distinct stages and surrounding conditions.
Using only one date for every species.
Every historical record is necessarily false.
The original descriptions may not support exact categories.

questions.prompt: How did the visitor guide change?
options: It guaranteed a permanent environmental trend.
It removed all information about flowering.
It described a likely flowering period rather than a guaranteed date.
It copied old dates without explanation.

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of exhibiting both kinds of records?
options: To show what different records can help explain.
To prove that old records should always be preferred.
To demonstrate that the new forms guarantee accuracy.
To make visitors classify every plant.

questions.prompt: What does retrospective mean in the context of retrospectively?
Which statement best expresses the author's argument?
options: Old dates alone establish environmental causes.
New observations make all earlier records useless.
Long-term records are most informative when their methods and limitations remain understandable.
A flowering calendar must predict exact dates.
questions.explanation_ja: 観測方法と限界が重要。
